name: Heavy oil upgrading (in-field)
principle: Upgrading is done near or in the reservoir to cut viscosity before transport. THAI's in-situ combustion upgraded oil by 3 to 7 API points at Kerrobert, and a nanocatalyst pilot in Colombia raised API from 11.6° to 13.4° while viscosity fell from 39,987 cP to 11,734 cP.

process_steps.name: Heat or catalyse heavy oil in place

source.note: In Situ Combustion Ltd, Toe-to-Heel Air Injection (THAI) brochure (field results to March 2022)
Wikipedia, Heavy crude oil, read 25 October 2026 (secondary source)

performance.metric: API gravity gain from CAPRI catalytic upgrading
performance.basis: Laboratory microreactor at 350-425 C and 20 barg for 9.2 min: 2-7 API gain and 42-82% viscosity reduction on a 13 API feed.

source.note: Hart et al., CAPRI in-situ upgrading (I&EC Research 2013), read 2026-11-17

advantages: Smaller diluent needs and easier transport
limitations: Few pilots; Wikipedia's heavy crude page does not cover upgrading

reference_plants.name: Long Lake SAGD with in-field upgrader (Nexen, later CNOOC), Alberta
reference_plants.capacity: design 72,000 bpd bitumen (SAGD + integrated in-field upgrader); operator guided 38,000-45,000 bpd for 2011

source.note: Reuters, 16 Nov 2010: "Long Lake to produce between 38,000 and 45,000 barrels per day of bitumen next year, less than the 72,000 bpd it is designed to produce". Upgrader reported fully operational Dec 2009 (The Globe and Mail, 10 Dec 2009); both read 2026-10-28

notes: Process provenance: Documents the bitumen upgrading process train and equipment - distillation/fractionation with diluent recovery, residue conversion above 400 C by coking (carbon rejection) and/or hydroconversion (hydrogen addition), catalytic hydrotreating for sulphur/nitrogen/metals removal, sulphur recovery to elemental sulphur, and blending of distillates into synthetic crude.
